Manchester United have triggered the one-year option in captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract, extending his stay at the club until 2028. As reported by BBC Sport on Friday, the 32-year-old’s previous deal was due to expire at the end of the current season. Sources say both the club and the player agreed it was in their mutual interest to activate the clause now. The decision means overseas clubs will be unable to approach Fernandes when the transfer window opens on 1 January. Without the extension, he would have been free to negotiate a pre-contract with teams outside England from that date. Fernandes confirmed earlier this week that talks over a brand-new long-term contract had been paused. Sources indicate those discussions are expected to resume once United’s league position improves. Pochettino seeks lucky break at crisis-hit Man Utd Osimhen wants United summer move, against Jan exit EPL: Fernandes laments Man Utd’s frequent managerial sackings The Portugal international has been a key figure at Old Trafford since joining from Sporting Lisbon in 2020 and has served as club captain in recent seasons. He had previously been offered new terms by the club but chose to put formal negotiations on hold amid the team’s difficult start to the campaign. By taking up the option, United have secured their skipper for an extra year while giving both sides more time to reach agreement on a longer deal in the future.
